full_judgment: 16. The Company's further allegation that the Board resolution approving share transfer is forged according to handwriting expert's report and, as such, the share transfer is invalid. Given the factual background of transfer of shares that all the works relating to transfer of shares from the two original shareholders (transferees) in favour of these two petitioners, including payment of consideration money, were done by the father of the petitioners as the then Chairman of the Company, the normal presumption would be that the father would not put his forged signature thereon. Moreover, it is the settled principle of law that a handwriting expert's report is not conclusive evidence, for, the Apex Court has viewed the handwriting expert's report to be a frail piece of evidence and, therefore, it does not carry much weight. In the case of Bhagwan Kaur vs Shri Maharaj Krishan Sharma, reported in ILR (1974) SC 10, it was held that "... that the evidence of a handwriting expert unlike that of a fingerprint expert is generally of a frail character and its fallibilities have been quite often noticed. The courts should therefore be wary to give too much weight to the evidence of the handwriting expert. The conclusions based upon mere comparison of handwriting must at best be indecisive and yield to the positive evidence in the case."
